findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the back storage room off the kitchen (water heater storage closet) to have bagged flour and boxed powdered foods to be stored in the unfinished space. The ceiling is not tiled and the floor is not coved. There is slight water seepage occurring around the floor. The room was previously observed with mouse droppings around the floor. Today, no droppings are observed, however, the space should have no food stored within or should have food protected if it is going to be used for food storage. Use large plastic storage tubs if you are going to continue to use the space for food storage. Provide storage bins that can be contained and are plastic or change the storage location of powdered foods.

Several food contact surfaces in the kitchen are thickly coated with accumulated dust and grease. The baffles of the hood system are coated in a layer of dust (baffles over the chicken broaster units). The broaster units themselves are observed to be coated with accumulated grease as is the surrounding floor and wall. See that the baffles are being routinely cleaned at a frequency that allows them to be maintained free of accumulated dust and grease.  After the baffles are clean, see that the baffles are cleaned a single one at a time and then moved down so that they maintain them clean. Clean the area surrounding the broaster (wall, floor, and attached plumbing).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

The dish machine was observed to measure 0ppm chlorine during today’s inspection. The PIC was informed and trouble-shot the machine. findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Upon arrival inspector observed an employee outside in front of the building on break; the employee had a single use glove on his hand. When the employee entered the kitchen he proceeded to the dish area. When inspector tried to speak with the employee about proper glove use and handwashing, he removed one glove to reveal another single use glove underneath. The glove was worn due to a bandage covered sore on one of his hands. Employee stated he was just doing dishes but was advised he needed to wash his hands upon entering the kitchen regardless of what task he is preparing to complete and that he must also wash his hands between tasks (i.e. going between handling dirty dishes and clean dishes, etc.). The employee quickly washed his hands with improper technique while still wearing a glove on his hand. The glove was removed after handwashing. The employee then washed his hands again per request of inspector and once again did it quickly and without proper technique. The employee was from a temp agency and was asked to leave by the GM who witnessed the whole incident. This particular worker will not be allowed to come back to work at the facility.

Employees must wash hands properly whenever hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, upon entering the kitchen, and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Gloves are intended for one use and must be changed when soiled, torn, or an interruption in task occurs.

findings.comment:
750.650a - A) Slicers used for cheese bread and dessert pizzas were observed with food contact surface sitting on cardboard pizza box soiled with grease. Although it was the inner, food contact surface of a pizza box that was used, it is not a good practice to store food contact surfaces on cardboard. It is not smooth or easily cleanable, and if not changed frequently will hold grease/debris and pose a potential risk for cross contamination. GM removed the cardboard from the area and took slicers to dish to go through ware washing.

B) Shelf above the staging area for cooked pizzas/beneath the order window had peeling paint along the edge, and the underneath surface was soiled and not smooth to the touch. Clean and repaint the shelf.

findings.citation_text:
750.830 - A) Colander in chicken prep area was soiled with buildup within holes and along outer bottom edge. Thoroughly pre-clean, and soak if necessary, the colander and all other equipment prior to running through the dish machine. Colander was placed in dirty dish area to go through ware washing.

B) Stuck on food debris was observed on a pizza spatula where metal meets the handle. Spatula was stored in a pan with other clean spatulas. GM removed the spatula in question and all spatulas in contact with the soiled spatula and took items to dish area for ware washing.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.
Repair the process as many times as necessary to ensure all surfaces are properly cleaned and sanitized.

B) (R) Wall beneath 3 part sink and underneath surfaces of the 3 part sink basins were soiled with splash/general buildup.
Caulk at 3 part sink and wall juncture was moldy.

C) (R) Acoustic tiles over fountain soda machine need to be changed to smooth, cleanable tiles (remaining from pre-opening inspection).

D) Bottom section of the wall behind chemical buckets at dish machine was soiled with splash.

E) Underside of chicken prep sink was soiled with splash. 

F) Hole was observed in the wall behind the door in the furnace room. Repair the wall (consider installing a door stop to reduce chance of further damage)

Clean the walls in the aforementioned areas, the general surfaces on the underside of sinks, and replace the moldy caulk.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle without a label was observed in the chicken prep area. Test strip was used to verify the chemical was sanitizer (200ppm quat).
GM labeled the bottle as to the contents.

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Wet mops were observed in the mopsink. GM moved mops to designated storage area to allow for proper drying.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly.
Wet mops can serve as a food/water source for pest - be careful with wet mop storage.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets tested below 200ppm quat (0-100ppm). Solution was checked at the dispenser and was observed at 200ppm. Sani-bucket solutions were remade to be at proper concentration.

When running sanitizer for the buckets, allow the solution to flow through the line for several seconds prior to filing buckets. Use test strips to verify sanitizing concentration (150-400ppm). Change solutions every 2 to 4o hours or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled. Clean out buckets daily and maintain clean. Grimy buildup in buckets can cause issues with sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) inside ice machine (mold) - 1. upper left side of metal baffle attached to ceiling & 2. ceiling on left side of opening where ice comes out
B) inside dish machine (general buildup - ceiling and bottom);
C) can opener blade (food debris);   and
D) soda nozzles/diffusers (mold).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - A) Knife holder above 3 part sink was soiled with splash/sticky buildup on front and back. Clean the knife holder as needed and maintain clean.

B) Large slicer was observed stored between the wall and crevice of the knife holder above the 3 part sink. Find a new place to store the slicer. The space between the wall and the knife holder is not considered a clean surface for storage unless it can be guaranteed that staff are cleaning/sanitizing all surfaces of the wall and knife holder daily.

C) Plastic tubs used for storage of clean lids, utensils, and equipment were soiled with food crumbs/general debris in the bottom. Clean storage tubs as needed and maintain clean. Consider covering tubs to help minimize crumb/debris accumulation between cleaning/sanitizing of tubs.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - A) Paper towels were not dispensing at handsink dispenser. Manager just changed the roll. Paper towels were adjusted to allow for dispensing. Towels were still difficult to dispense. A stack of folded paper towels were also provided to allow for proper handwashing. NOTE: If staff have to continually push the lever of the dispenser, it is not necessarily conducive to proper handwashing and use of a barrier for touching unclean surfaces once handwashing process is completed.

B) Kitchen handsink basin had some grimy buildup. Also, general buildup was present around the faucet handles.
Clean the handsinks and all related fixtures as needed and maintain clean.

Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean

750.1210 & 1220 - A) Wall behind dish machine was soiled with general buildup.

B) Wall beneath 3 part sink and underneath surfaces of the 3 part sink basins were soiled with splash/general buildup.
Caulk at 3 part sink and wall juncture was moldy.

Clean the walls in the aforementioned areas, the general surfaces on the underside of the 3 part sink, and replace the moldy caulk.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: Proofing racks are not 6 inches above the floor. Observed proofing rack full of crusts on the floor (covered with a food grade bag) in the kitchen. 750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food. Rack was moved to shelf.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The drop guard on the ice machine is soiled and the can opener blade is soiled upon arrival. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.  The drop guard and the can opener were both properly cleaned.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: A tub holding clean utensils at the dish area had crumbs and soil in the bottom. 750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Bus tub and utensils were washed immediately.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Floors are soiled in areas around legs of equipment, under shelves and along base boards. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain clean.
Floor and cove area next to the walk in and behind the prep cooler is in disrepair. 750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Hood vent over pizza ovens has some dust soil and grease accumulation. Also, ceiling over the walk in condenser has some soil on the vent grates. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
